notes: §1985:VI.6.2.3 GR5 gives exponentiation three rules: a) 'If the value of an expression to be raised to a power is zero, the exponent must have a value greater than zero. Otherwise, the size error condition exists', b) of a positive and a negative real result the positive one is returned, c) 'If no real number exists as the result of the evaluation, the size error condition exists'. NumericRenderer.Power lowers every ** to the exact power (CobolExact.Pow, integer exponent) or the native one (PowNativeReal), and both ask the one screen CobolIntrinsics.CheckPowRule6 first; no edition reaches it differently. a) conforms (0 ** 0 and 0 ** -1 are size errors, 0 ** 2 and 0 ** 0.5 are 0) and b) conforms (4 ** 0.5 is 2, 16 ** 0.25 is 2: the principal root); the witness runs one case of each. c) is implemented as the later, stricter rule: CheckPowRule6 raises the size error for EVERY negative base with a non-integer exponent (§2023:8.8.1.2 GR6 c: 'If the value of an expression to be raised to a power is less than zero, the evaluation of the exponent shall result in an integer'), where 1985 raises it only when no real result exists. (-32) ** 0.2 is the fifth root of -32, the real number -2 (the exponent is the exact decimal 1/5), so 1985 returns -2 and the compiler takes the SIZE ERROR phrase; with no phrase (a condition, IF NB ** 0.2 < 0) the run unit ends with a fatal EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION although 1985 defines the value. (-4) ** 0.5, which has no real result, is correctly a size error. The rule's change record names this difference; no 1985 arm exists for it.

next.reason: Rules a and b are kept in §2023:8.8.1.2 GR6 a) and b) (zero base needs a positive exponent; of a positive and a negative real result the positive is returned), the size error condition still raised (EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION is set but checking is off for a 1985 program). Rule c differs: 1985 'If no real number exists as the result of the evaluation, the size error condition exists'; 2023 'If the value of an expression to be raised to a power is less than zero, the evaluation of the exponent shall result in an integer. Otherwise ... the size error condition is raised'. (-32) ** 0.2 has the real result -2, so 1985 returns -2 while 2023 raises size error. The 0 ** 0 rules of 8.8.1.4.4 and 8.8.1.5.4 belong to standard-binary and standard-decimal arithmetic, which a 1985 program never selects.
